subject: Implementation credits vs. recurring credits — Sunrise Health (HSM/KMS/residency)
messages:
From: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@sunrisehealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@sunrisehealth.com
Date: 2027-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Implementation credits vs. recurring credits — Sunrise Health (HSM/KMS/residency)

Thanks Markus — quick note from procurement: Sunrise is comfortable committing to the 18-month volume forecast we shared, but the finance team needs clarity on how you plan to apply the implementation credit for HSM seats and the residency onboarding fee.

Specifically: can we get a clear amortization schedule (monthly credit applied vs one-time offset) and an explanation of whether the HSM seat fee is considered capex (one-time) or ongoing licensing for your billing? Our auditors require the invoice treatment to match the contract language.

Also, DataSafe (copied) asked for a short note on evidence delivery: what format will audit logs and attestation artifacts be delivered in, and what milestones trigger the credits?

Appreciate if you can send a compact table and a short summary by EOD Thursday.

—Amelia
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@sunrisehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, DataSafe Legal <datalegal@datasafe.io>
Date: 2027-06-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Implementation credits vs. recurring credits — Sunrise Health (HSM/KMS/residency)

Amelia — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a short workbook and a draft amortization table. High level summary below: 

- HSM seat fee: treated as a one-time implementation/licensing fee on Redwood's invoice for year 1. For accounting purposes we can show it as capex on your side; however, we propose a monthly amortization credit that runs against your hosted usage charges across the first 12 months (effectively turning the net cash impact into a monthly OPEX-like reduction).
- Residency onboarding (networking, private control plane) and auditlog integration: we treat as implementation work. We propose a milestone-credit model: 50% credit applied after onboarding completion and evidence handoff; remaining 50% amortized over 6 months as credits against monthly service invoices.
- KMS integration: if you choose Redwood-managed KMS seats vs BYOK, there is a smaller implementation fee that we recommend amortizing across 6 months.

Suggested commercial concession for Sunrise given the 18-month commit: 40% of HSM seat fee credited back as an up-front invoice credit (applied in month 1) plus the remaining 60% amortized monthly over 12 months. This preserves vendor cashflow while giving you immediate discount protection.

I flagged details for Ben (pricing) and Laura (legal) to confirm language. Mina from Solutions Ops included evidence delivery notes in the workbook. If this fits, we can convert to contract language for DocuSign and map the invoice line items.

Best,
Markus
VP, GTM Pricing
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@sunrisehealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-03T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Implementation credits vs. recurring credits — Sunrise Health (HSM/KMS/residency)

Quick notes from pricing: the numbers in the workbook assume standard HSM licensing at list. Two optional levers to share if Sunrise pushes back: 

1) Early-commit tier: if Sunrise converts MRR forecasts to an annual prepaid commit at signing, we can increase the up-front credit on HSM seats to 60% and cap the monthly amortization to 6 months.
2) Usage floor: set a conservative monthly usage floor (e.g., 65% of forecast) below which credits stop applying. That protects us from churn risk.

Both levers are negotiable; recommend we present both to Amelia as options with clear pros/cons. Happy to run a revised workbook for either scenario.

—Ben
From: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@sunrisehealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@sunrisehealth.com, DataSafe Legal <datalegal@datasafe.io>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-05T11:26:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Implementation credits vs. recurring credits — Sunrise Health (HSM/KMS/residency)

Thanks Markus/Ben — the options look reasonable. A couple of clarifying asks from finance and legal: 

- Can you confirm the exact invoice line description you will use for the "HSM seat credit" so our AP can map to the right GL code? (AP wants a single line item name to match to the PO.)
- For the evidence handoff milestone, DataSafe asks that audit logs be delivered in newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) and that attestations include a signed PDF with a timestamp. Is that supported?
- Regarding the early-commit tier: if we do annual prepaid, what is the timeline for Redwood to return unused credits if actual usage is below the prepaid amount?

If you can confirm by Monday we'll circulate to internal approvers.

—Amelia
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@sunrisehealth.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, DataSafe Legal <datalegal@datasafe.io>
Date: 2027-06-07T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Implementation credits vs. recurring credits — Sunrise Health (HSM/KMS/residency)

Amelia — answering your points below: 

1) Invoice line description: "Redwood HSM Seat Implementation Credit (DEAL-7831)" — we will include the PO reference and a short memo on the invoice to ease GL mapping.

2) Evidence delivery: yes, we can deliver audit logs as ndjson via a secure SFTP link or an encrypted archive in your private bucket. Attestations will be provided as signed PDFs with ISO 8601 timestamps; we can include hashing metadata for verification. Mina is copying the exact file naming convention in the attached workbook.

3) Unused prepaid credits: for annual prepay, we propose a 90-day reconciliation window at the end of the first year. Unused prepaid credits can either be rolled forward to cover subsequent usage (up to the 18-month term) or refunded pro rata minus any third-party HSM pass-through costs. We'll outline the math in a contract schedule. If Sunrise prefers a refund guardrail, we can cap refunds to the residual pass-through costs only.

Next steps: if these items are acceptable, Markus will update the commercial exhibit and we can route a short amendment through DocuSign. If DataSafe needs additional attestation language, please send a redline and we'll respond.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts
Redwood Inference
